Acceleration vs Entropy

If change is accelerating, how does this relate to the principle of entropy, and the tendency of the universe to decay?

Local Complexity, Global Disorder

Ecological & cultural inheritance accelerate local complexity by riding energy gradients — increasing global entropy while building temporary islands of order.

Entropy (Global Backdrop) Local Complexity (Life, Minds, Cities) Acceleration via Inheritance Energy Throughput (The Cost)
  • Second Law: in closed systems, entropy increases.
  • Open systems can decrease local entropy by exporting disorder to the environment.
  • Cosmic endgame: eventual heat death if no new gradients.
  • Living systems maintain low entropy states by continuous energy throughput.
  • Neural/cultural “order” is dynamic and energy-hungry.
  • Complexity is temporary, process-maintained structure.
  • Ecological inheritance: modified niches (soils, wetlands) scaffold faster adaptation.
  • Cultural inheritance: writing, institutions, code → cumulative culture accelerates innovation.
  • Compounding feedback: each layer speeds up the next.
  • More complexity ⇒ higher free-energy rate density.
  • Societies accelerate entropy export (fossil → renewables shifts change the profile, not the rule).
  • Acceleration follows available gradients; stalls when gradients decline.
Clausius–Boltzmann formulation; dissipative structures. Schrödinger’s “negative entropy”; Prigogine’s far-from-equilibrium order. Niche Construction Theory; Dual Inheritance Theory. Lotka–Odum “maximum power”; Chaisson’s free-energy rate density.

Entropy (Global Backdrop)

  • Second Law: in closed systems, entropy increases.
  • Open systems can decrease local entropy by exporting disorder to the environment.
  • Cosmic endgame: eventual heat death if no new gradients.

Open‑system accounting

dS_total = dS_system + dS_env ≥ 0
local order ⇒ dS_system < 0 requires dS_env ≫ 0

Anchors: Clausius–Boltzmann formulation; dissipative structures.

Local Complexity (Life, Minds, Cities)

  • Living systems maintain low entropy states by continuous energy throughput.
  • Neural/cultural “order” is dynamic and energy‑hungry.
  • Complexity is temporary, process‑maintained structure.

Anchors: Schrödinger’s “negative entropy”; Prigogine’s far‑from‑equilibrium order.

Acceleration via Inheritance

  • Ecological inheritance: modified niches (soils, wetlands) scaffold faster adaptation.
  • Cultural inheritance: writing, institutions, code → cumulative culture accelerates innovation.
  • Compounding feedback: each layer speeds up the next.

Anchors: Niche Construction Theory; Dual Inheritance Theory.

Energy Throughput (The Cost)

  • More complexity ⇒ higher free‑energy rate density.
  • Societies accelerate entropy export (fossil → renewables shifts change the profile, not the rule).
  • Acceleration follows available gradients; stalls when gradients decline.

Anchors: Lotka–Odum “maximum power”; Chaisson’s free‑energy rate density.

Putting It Together

  • No contradiction: Local acceleration coexists with global entropy increase.
  • Thermo‑compliance: Complexity persists only by burning gradients (sunlight, chemical, technological).
  • Fragility: When energy flows falter, complex structures decay and inheritance chains break.
